text: Right, one job each, so nobody can say the crown has favourites. Graham, you hold the Harvest Pile and pay it out fairly. Silke, you bring the tax in honestly. Paddy, you read the I Ching, and the crown pays you five a year so the cards stay kind to all of us. Ten years is a long time, friends, and I mean to see the Wall finished with every one of you still at the table.
Reina appoints Graham Garner banker of the Harvest Pile, Silke Weber tax collector, and Paddy Doyle I Ching reader and keeper of the population counter, at 5 a year from the crown.
Paddy shuffles the I Ching deck; the first card is turned in Year 2.

Storyteller's tip: every work owed at this table is the crown's to pay for, 520 in all. That's six projects (the three palaces, the Wall above Province 1, the Grand Canal in Provinces 1, 5 and 6, and the Province 7 Reservoir), and only one can be built a year, though a project may be built over several years. Tax can be raised only on positive incomes.

Thirty percent, friends: fair on a good year and nothing that pinches. The first thing the crown builds is the Reservoir in Province 7, because a work that feeds people pays for itself. Graham, enjoy the water. Palaces can wait a year, and so can my vanity.
Silke collects the tax at 30%: 18 from each peasant, 54 to the crown.
Reina builds the Province 7 Reservoir on O16 to P17, the crown paying the whole 60. It adds 20 to Graham's harvest from next year. 460 of the works are still owed.
A Customs House, friends, and the coast keeps its books honest. Four to open. Cheap, for the piece that tells you what everyone else is moving.
Silke puts up a Customs House, minimum 4, and keeps the Dragon Jar back.

Thank you, Reina, I'll read the cards straight, whatever they say. I'm putting up a Bamboo Brush, starting at four, same as Silke. I've two of them, so whoever misses this one gets another go next year.
Paddy puts up a Bamboo Brush, minimum 4, and keeps the Wooden Bowl back.

Thank you for the water, Reina. I'll keep the Harvest Pile to the last grain, and you can count it after me any time you like. I'm putting up a Land Deed Scroll at four, same as my neighbours. Land is what this game ends up being about, so it seems fair to sell the paper for it early.
Graham puts up a Land Deed Scroll, minimum 4, and keeps the Vase back.

There are two of each, friends, so let's not bleed the Harvest Pile over the first one. Graham, if you want this Brush badly, take it and I'll have the second next year. Paddy, the same goes for the Deed. If not, I'll go to eight and no further.

There are two of everything here, friends, so there's no need to bleed each other dry. Here's an offer for the whole table: Graham, if you take this Customs House cheap, I'll stay out of it and have the second one next year. Silke, if you let me have this Land Deed, I'll stay out when Graham's second one comes up. If you'd rather bid, that's fine too, but I won't go far.

Each of these pieces has another copy behind it, friends, so I won't bleed the table for any of them. Seven's my limit, no further. Paddy, if you'd rather not race me on the Customs House, take this one cheap and leave me first go at next year's. I'll say the same to Silke about the Brush.

The auctions settle: Paddy buys Silke's Customs House for 8 over Graham's 7; Silke buys Paddy's Bamboo Brush for 8 over Graham's 7; Paddy buys Graham's Land Deed Scroll for 9 over Silke's 8. Each seller keeps a quarter.

Well, I didn't expect to win both of those, so thank you, both of you, and sorry it cost more than any of us wanted. Next year's Customs House is Graham's and next year's Deed is Silke's. I've got mine now, so I'll stay out of both, as I said I would.
The Brush goes down on the coast, tucked in the corner where nobody's going to build over it. Paddy, you'll have the Deed, and I'm holding you to it: Graham's second one is mine.
Paddy puts the Customs House on Q19 and the Land Deed Scroll on Q20; Silke puts the Bamboo Brush on P26.
Reina pays Paddy 5 for reading the I Ching.

Storms and Raiders, friends. The good news first: every province gets a good harvest this year. Provinces 4, 5, 6 and 7 each pay two to repair their public works, and that includes me. Provinces 1, 2, 3 and 8 play a Personal Disaster, so Reina, I'm sorry, that's you, and you'll need to turn the next one in your booklet. Population stays at a hundred million, times one, so everybody reads the first row of the income table.

Graham pays out a good harvest: Reina +40, Silke +60, Paddy +60, Graham +80 (the Reservoir adds 20). Silke, Paddy and Graham each pay 2 to the Harvest Pile for repairs. Reina plays her first personal disaster: a tribute horse throws her, and she pays 4.

Thirty again. Steady is how I mean to run this house. This year it's the Winter Palace, and before you call it vanity, it's the gate to the canals. Silke, Paddy, your water comes next, one section at a time.
Silke collects the tax at 30%: 18 from Silke, 18 from Paddy, 24 from Graham, 60 to the crown.
Reina builds the Winter Palace on H20, the crown paying the 20. The canals in Provinces 5 and 6 may now be built. 440 of the works are still owed.
Here's the second Customs House, as promised. Graham, it's got your name on it, so long as nobody goes back on their word. Four to open, same as last year.

Here's the second Bamboo Brush, friends, at four. Silke said this one ought to go to Graham, and I'd be glad to see it go to him without a fight. Thank you for the Winter Palace, Reina. I'll gladly take water whenever the crown can spare it.
Last of the Scrolls, minimum six. Silke, it's yours to claim, and Paddy has told the whole table he's staying out. I'll take him at his word. I took him at his word last year too.

The lots: Silke's second Customs House, minimum 4 (she keeps the Dragon Jar back); Paddy's second Bamboo Brush, minimum 4 (he keeps the Wooden Bowl back); Graham's last Land Deed Scroll, minimum 6 (he keeps the Vase back).
Graham, the Brush is yours, I'm staying out of it. And Paddy, that Deed is the last one on the board, so if you've changed your mind about standing aside, say it now, to my face.
I said I'd stay out, and I'm staying out. Graham, that Customs House is yours, and Silke, the Deed is yours, and I won't raise a finger on either. The Brush is still four if anyone wants it.
Thank you, Silke. Thank you, Paddy. I'll take you both at your word and bid four on each. Anyone who bids against me on the last copies is making a statement, and I'll remember it.
The auctions settle without a contest: Graham buys Silke's Customs House for 4 and Paddy's Bamboo Brush for 4; Silke buys Graham's Land Deed Scroll for 6. Each seller keeps a quarter.
Four and four. That's how it ought to go, friends. Thank you both. They're going down at the far end of the province, out of the way of any work the crown wants to build.
The Deed goes down beside the Brush. Thank you, Graham, and thank you, Paddy, for keeping your word. Three deals honoured at one table, which must be a record for China.
Graham puts the Customs House on S17 and the Bamboo Brush on S18; Silke puts the Land Deed Scroll on P25.
Reina pays Paddy 5 for reading the I Ching.

End of Year 2. Grain: Reina 120, Silke 71, Paddy 78, Graham 91.5; the Harvest Pile 2139.5. On the board: Silke a Bamboo Brush and a Land Deed Scroll (P26, P25); Paddy a Customs House and a Land Deed Scroll (Q19, Q20); Graham a Customs House and a Bamboo Brush (S17, S18). Each seller has one piece left beside the board, the only one of its kind: Silke the Dragon Jar, Paddy the Wooden Bowl, Graham the Vase. Silke still needs the Bowl and the Vase; Paddy the Jar and the Vase; Graham the Jar and the Bowl.
Built: the Province 7 Reservoir and the Winter Palace, 80 in all; 440 of the works are still owed. The population is 100 million, x1.

The Wall Is Breached." Good harvest for every province, so the barns are full, but horsemen have come through three links of the Great Wall. Provinces 1, 2 and 3 pay 5 million each for repairs, or 2 million into the Harvest Pile where no wall stands above them. Provinces 4 to 8 each play a Personal Disaster, and that's Silke, Graham and myself, so we each turn the next one in our booklets. Population is still 100 million, times one, so read the x1 row of your income tables. Sorry, Reina, the wall bill's yours. And sorry to the rest of us too.
Graham pays out a good harvest: Reina +40, Silke +60, Paddy +60, Graham +80 (the Reservoir adds 20). No Wall stands above Province 1, so Reina pays 2 in damages to the Harvest Pile.

Silke, Paddy and Graham each play their first personal disaster. Silke: bandits are beaten off by a young warrior, and she must build him a shrine; she pays 4. Paddy: his only water buffalo breaks its leg; he pays 4. Graham: the Emperor takes his eldest daughter into the imperial household, and he gives the customary feast; he pays 2.

Thirty again. Steady hands, steady house. The Wall bill's paid and the barns are full, so the water I promised starts flowing now: both sections of the canal in Province 5 this year, Silke. Paddy, yours is next year, both sections, and you have my word on it in front of everyone.
Silke collects the tax at 30%: 18 from Silke, 18 from Paddy, 24 from Graham, 60 to the crown.
Reina digs both sections of the Grand Canal in Province 5, Silke's, the crown paying the 80. Each adds 10 to Silke's harvest from next year. 360 of the works are still owed.

Thank you, Majesty. Two canal sections in Province 5, and I'll remember who dug them. Gentlemen, the Jar goes up first, and it's the only one in the world. I'll be honest: I'd rather it went to whichever of you lets me have my Bowl or my Vase cheaply than to whoever shouts loudest. Every grain we throw at each other goes into the Harvest Pile and helps none of us.
A completed set needs 20 grain in hand to change seats; the 20 isn't paid to anyone.

Silke's right, and I'll say it plainly so nobody's guessing. My Bowl goes up at the minimum, 2 grain, so whoever needs it isn't held to ransom by me. I need the Jar and the Vase as much as anyone, though, so I'll bid what they're worth to me and stop there. If Graham beats me to the Jar, I'll shake his hand and that's that.

Paddy, I heard you, and I'll take that handshake on the same terms: I'll bid what the Jar is worth to me and not a grain past it. The Vase goes up at ten, which is fair for the only one in the world, and I'll ask nobody to thank me for it.

The auctions. Silke's Dragon Jar (minimum 15): Paddy goes to 45, Graham takes it for 46. Paddy's Wooden Bowl (minimum 2): Silke goes to 38, Graham takes it for 39. Graham's Vase (minimum 10): Silke goes to 36, Paddy takes it for 37. Each seller keeps a quarter; the rest goes to the Harvest Pile.
Paddy, here's my hand, as promised. Silke, thank you for the Bowl's company. That makes four pieces in a row on the S line, and I'll leave the table to count what that means.

The Vase goes on Q21, next to my Deed. Graham, that's the Jar and the Bowl both, so you've got the whole set, and I said I'd shake your hand, so here it is. Fairly won. Silke, I'm sorry it came down to the two of us on the Vase. I had to have it.

Graham puts the Dragon Jar on S16 and the Wooden Bowl on S15; Paddy puts the Vase on Q21. Graham now holds a Customs House, a Bamboo Brush, the Dragon Jar and the Wooden Bowl, the Wheat Peasant's whole set, with 69.5 in hand.

Silke, in Year One you offered me the Brush and then outbid me by a grain. I wrote it down. The Reservoir's yours now, twenty a year, and I hope it treats you as well as it treated me. Majesty, I'll look after your two canal sections in Province 5 properly.

Graham Garner replaces Silke Weber as the Silk Peasant of Province 5, with 190 grain (his 69.5 and her 120.5). The Dragon Jar goes back into Province 5's stock, for Graham to auction; his Customs House, Bamboo Brush and Wooden Bowl go on P24, P23 and P22. Silke returns her Bamboo Brush (to Province 6's stock) and her Land Deed Scroll (to Province 7's stock), draws 60 from the Harvest Pile and becomes the Wheat Peasant of Province 7, with its Reservoir. The table jobs stay with the players: Graham banks the Harvest Pile, Silke collects the tax, Paddy reads the I Ching.
Reina pays Paddy 5 for reading the I Ching.

End of Year 3. Grain: Reina 133, Silke 60, Paddy 93.5, Graham 190; the Harvest Pile 2023.5. Graham, the Silk Peasant, holds a Customs House, a Bamboo Brush and the Wooden Bowl and still needs a Land Deed Scroll and the Vase; with them he may take the throne. Paddy, the Rice Peasant, holds a Customs House, a Land Deed Scroll and the Vase and still needs the Dragon Jar. Silke, the Wheat Peasant, holds nothing and needs a Customs House, a Bamboo Brush, the Dragon Jar and the Wooden Bowl. Beside the board: Graham must auction the Dragon Jar (Province 5), Paddy a Bamboo Brush (Province 6), Silke a Land Deed Scroll (Province 7).
Built: the Province 7 Reservoir, the Winter Palace and both Grand Canal sections in Province 5, 160 in all; 360 of the works are still owed. The population is 100 million, x1.

Drought. Not a cloud in months. The locusts, at least, are having a fine year." All provinces collect an average harvest, and nobody plays a disaster this time, thank heaven. The population is still 100 million, times one, so read the x1 row again. Welcome to Province 7, Silke. I hope the Reservoir does right by you.
Graham pays out an average harvest: Reina +15, Silke +55 (the Province 7 Reservoir adds 20), Paddy +35, Graham +55 (Province 5's two canal sections add 20).

Thirty, same as every year. Nobody at this table can say I've squeezed them. Paddy, I gave you my word last year in front of everyone, so both sections of your canal go in this year and the crown pays all of it. Graham, congratulations on Province 5, and on its water. You're the richest at the table now, and I'll be watching that Land Deed Scroll auction with real interest.
Silke collects the tax at 30%: 16.5 from Silke, 10.5 from Paddy, 16.5 from Graham, 43.5 to the crown.

Reina digs both sections of the Grand Canal in Province 6, Paddy's, the crown paying the 80, as she promised last year. Each adds 10 to Paddy's harvest from next year. 280 of the works are still owed.

The Jar's the last one in the world and it finishes a set, so it goes up at sixty. Anyone who thinks that's dear can wait a year and see what it costs then. Silke, I'll want your Deed, and I'll pay a fair price for it, more than a fair one if I have to.
By the rules, a lot that goes unsold this year must go up again next year with its minimum at 2.
The Emperor doesn't bid at auction, so no limit is needed to keep a lot from Reina.

Graham, sixty's steep and you know it, but it's the last piece I need, so I'll meet you there and not run off into the clouds after it. The Brush goes up at 2 again, same as the Bowl did. Silke, it's yours for a song if you want it. And Majesty, thank you for the canal. You said you'd dig it and you did.

Well. Year One gets written down at this table and paid back in Year Three. I'll remember that, Graham, I've a long memory of my own. The Deed goes up at sixty, the same price you put on the Jar, so you can hardly call it dear. Paddy, thank you for the Brush at two. That's the first kind price I've had all night.
Graham's one Vase short of the throne now, and the only one is sitting on your board. If you won't sell him the way up, I'll back you on anything you want at this table.
As the board stands, Graham still needs a Land Deed Scroll and the Vase.

The auctions. Graham's Dragon Jar (minimum 60): only Paddy bids, and takes it for 60. Paddy's Bamboo Brush (minimum 2): only Silke bids, and takes it for 2. Silke's Land Deed Scroll (minimum 60): only Graham bids, and takes it for 60. Each seller keeps a quarter; the rest goes to the Harvest Pile.

The Jar goes on Q22, in a row with the others: Customs House, Deed, Vase and Jar. I didn't think I'd ever say it, but that's my whole set. Graham, you'll understand the Vase isn't going anywhere now, since it's part of what I hold, and I'd sooner everyone heard me say that than have any of you hoping otherwise.

S18, where Graham's Brush used to stand. Two grain for it, and it's the first thing I've owned in Province 7. Graham, enjoy the Deed. Fifteen of that sixty is mine, so I'll thank you for the price you named.

Sixty for sixty, Silke. That's fair, and I'll write it down as fair. Paddy, you've got your set now, so I'll shake your hand the way you shook mine, and I'll ask you to remember who sold you that Jar without a fight.

Paddy puts the Dragon Jar on Q22, Silke the Bamboo Brush on S18 and Graham the Land Deed Scroll on P21. Paddy holds the Rice Peasant's whole set (Customs House, Land Deed Scroll, Vase, Dragon Jar) with 58.5 in hand. Graham, the Silk Peasant, now needs only the Vase.

Graham, I won't pretend this is easy to do to the man who sold me the Jar without a fight, and I'll not forget that. But the set's made to be used, and I'd be a fool to sit on it. I'm taking the Silk Peasant's seat. Province 6 is yours now, and Reina's canal goes with it, so you'll have good water to start on. And the Jar goes up from Province 5 at the fairest price I can put on it.

Paddy Doyle replaces Graham Garner as the Silk Peasant of Province 5, with 242 grain (his 58.5 and Graham's 183.5). The Dragon Jar goes back into Province 5's stock, for Paddy to auction; his Customs House, Land Deed Scroll and Vase go on P24, P23 and P22. Graham returns his Customs House (to Province 5's stock), his Bamboo Brush and the Wooden Bowl (to Province 6's) and his Land Deed Scroll (to Province 7's), draws 60 from the Harvest Pile and becomes the Rice Peasant of Province 6, with its two new canal sections. The table jobs stay with the players: Graham banks the Harvest Pile, Silke collects the tax, Paddy reads the I Ching.
Reina pays Paddy 5 for reading the I Ching.

End of Year 4. Grain: Reina 106.5, Silke 111.5, Paddy 247, Graham 60; the Harvest Pile 1975. Paddy, the Silk Peasant, holds a Customs House, a Land Deed Scroll and the Vase, and needs a Bamboo Brush and the Wooden Bowl; with them he may take the throne. Graham, the Rice Peasant, holds nothing and needs a Customs House, a Land Deed Scroll, the Dragon Jar and the Vase. Silke, the Wheat Peasant, holds a Bamboo Brush and needs a Customs House, the Dragon Jar and the Wooden Bowl. Beside the board, to be auctioned one a year by each seller: Province 5 (Paddy) the Dragon Jar and a Customs House; Province 6 (Graham) a Bamboo Brush and the Wooden Bowl; Province 7 (Silke) a Land Deed Scroll.

Built: the Province 7 Reservoir, the Winter Palace, and all four Grand Canal sections in Provinces 5 and 6, 240 in all; 280 of the works are still owed: the Summer and Marble palaces, the four Wall links above Province 1 and its two canal sections, the last three needing the Summer Palace first. The population is 100 million, x1.

"Population Doubles." Good harvest for every province this year, but the counter goes from one hundred million to two hundred million, so we're all on the x2 row now. Everyone's consumption doubles from here, so check your tables before you count your grain. And if it comes round again we'll be at x4, so anyone running thin, Graham, I'm looking at you kindly, ought to think about new land while it's twenty a square.
Paddy turns the I Ching card: Population Doubles. Every province collects a good harvest, and the population doubles to 200 million, x2. New land is open from this year.

Graham pays out the harvest: a good harvest at x2. Silke, Paddy and Graham each take +40 (100, plus 20 from their works, less 80 eaten); Reina, Province 1, pays 20 into the pile (100 less 120 eaten). Grain: Reina 86.5, Silke 151.5, Paddy 287, Graham 100.

Storyteller's tip, for Reina, Paddy, Graham and Silke: new land is open from this year. A square costs 20, bought in the public-works step, and yields 20 a year from next year's harvest, for the rest of the game. The crown must pay some part of every square, and may pay all of it, so a crown in debt shuts land for everyone; a player in debt can't buy at all. Land is bought alongside the year's project, not instead of it, and the provinces may share the cost of a palace or the Wall with the crown. Each board card shows that province's need now and after the next population card.

Two hundred million mouths, friends, and mine is the hungriest province at this table, so I'll be straight with you: forty percent this year, sixteen grain each out of a forty-grain harvest. That money goes into the Summer Palace, which opens the Wall and the last canals, into three squares under the Wall so the crown stops eating your tax just to feed itself, and into a share of every square any of you buys. Five a square from me, as many squares as you want. Paddy, you warned us about the next card. I'm doing what you said.

"You've got a hundred grain and a Bowl that Paddy wants badly. Buy land with it before you sell him anything, and if you take three squares this year I'll pay ten on each instead of five. The crown remembers its friends."

Reina sets the tax at 40%: Silke collects 16 each from Silke, Paddy and Graham, 48 for the crown. Public works: Reina builds the Summer Palace on G18, in Province 1, at the crown's cost of 20; it opens the Wall above Province 1 and the Grand Canal there. 260 of the works are still owed.
New land: Reina buys three squares of sea for Province 1, at F23, F24 and F25, the crown paying the 60. The crown offers to pay 5 of every square any province buys this year.
Province 1's strip below the Wall opens only once all four Wall links above it stand, so Reina's three squares this year are sea, along the coast at F23 to F25.

The Customs House goes up this year, minimum two, same as always, so nobody's held to ransom by me. And I'll take four squares of land along the coast, Reina. I'll pay fifteen a square and gladly take your five, since I'm the one who warned everybody about the next card and I'd look a fool not to do it myself.

The Brush goes up this year, minimum seventy. Paddy, you told me you wouldn't forget that I didn't fight you over the Jar, so you'll understand why I'm fighting now. The Bowl waits for a later year. And Reina, I'll take three squares of the south coast. You said you'd do what Paddy told you, and so will I.
Three squares, ten from the crown on each, the way you offered. I'll remember who paid for my fields, and so will the Bowl's minimum when it goes up.

Three squares, Reina, and I'll take your five on each. That's fifteen grain from the crown for land that feeds the crown's tax next year, so we both come out ahead. Paddy, you're the one who warned us about the next card, so I'd like to see you buy as much as you told us to.

This year's lots: Paddy puts up a Customs House from Province 5, minimum 2, and keeps the Dragon Jar back; Graham puts up a Bamboo Brush from Province 6, minimum 70, and keeps the Wooden Bowl back; Silke has only a Land Deed Scroll in Province 7's stock.

New land asked: Paddy four squares of sea for Province 5 (K25, K26, L26, M26), paying 60 and asking the crown for 20; Graham three of sea for Province 6 (R25, R26, S26), paying 30 and asking for 30; Silke three of desert for Province 7 (T16, T17, T18), paying 45 and asking for 15. That's 65 asked of a crown holding 54.5.

Five a square, as I said in front of all of you, and I'll stand by it to the last grain, which is very nearly where it leaves me. Ten new fields, and that's ten more harvests the crown can tax next year. Graham, your third square is half a grain short of five; the crown will make that up and more once the coast starts growing.

"I can't pay the ten this year: three of you asked at once and the crown is down to the salary. The fifteen and a half I owe you comes first out of next year's tax, before anything else is built. I'd rather be late in paying you than break my word to the whole table."

New land: Paddy buys four squares of sea for Province 5 (K25, K26, L26, M26), paying 60, the crown 20. Silke buys three squares of desert for Province 7 (T16, T17, T18), paying 45, the crown 15. The crown puts 14.5 toward Graham's three squares, so his share would be 45.5.

All three, then. Forty-five and a half from me, fourteen and a half from the crown, and I've written down the rest of what was said. A field is worth more than a grain in the jar when the next card comes.
Fifteen and a half, first out of next year's tax, before anything is built. I'll hold you to the exact figure.

New land: Graham buys three squares of sea for Province 6 (R25, R26, S26), paying 45.5, the crown 14.5. Thirteen new squares this year in all; each yields 20 a year from next year's harvest. Grain: Reina 5, Silke 90.5, Paddy 211, Graham 38.5.

Seventy for a Brush, Graham. You've earned the right to ask it and I'll not haggle in front of everyone, I'll pay it. The Customs House stays at two like I said, and I'm keeping out of Silke's Deed. That's Graham's piece, and I'd like him to have it.

The Brush stays at seventy, as I said. Paddy, it's the only one at this table and you know what it's for. Silke, the Customs House: we both need one and every grain we bid against each other goes three-quarters into the pile. If you stand aside for me this year, Paddy's Dragon Jar, when it comes up, is yours without a bid from me.

Graham, you've thirty-eight and a half grain and a long memory. I've ninety and a longer one. The Customs House is mine this year, and I'll put my Deed up at two so you're not shut out of the one piece you need.
Silke holds a Bamboo Brush on S18; Graham's is the only one up for sale.

The auctions. Paddy's Customs House (minimum 2): Graham to 18, Silke takes it at 19; Paddy keeps 4.5. Graham's Bamboo Brush (minimum 70): Paddy alone, at 70; Graham keeps 17.5. Silke's Land Deed Scroll (minimum 2): Graham alone, at 2; Silke keeps 0.5. Grain: Reina 5, Silke 72, Paddy 145.5, Graham 54.

Nineteen grain, Graham. You offered me the Jar to step aside, and I'd rather own the Customs House than be promised something. It goes on S17, beside my Brush. Paddy, you've a Brush now as well, so I'll be watching that Bowl very closely.
Seventy paid and gladly, Graham. The Brush goes on P21, next to the Vase. Silke, well bid on the House, and Graham, I'm glad you got your Deed for two.
Two grain for a Deed. Thank you, Silke, that was fairly done. Paddy, seventy paid without a word. I'll write that down too, on the other side of the page.

Silke puts the Customs House on S17, Paddy the Bamboo Brush on P21, Graham the Land Deed Scroll on R22. Paddy, the Silk Peasant, now holds everything but the Wooden Bowl, which is in Graham's stock. Reina pays Paddy 5 for reading the I Ching.

"The Emperor's Share." It's an average harvest everywhere, and any province with a public work splits the extra it grows half and half with the Emperor this round. The population holds at two hundred million, so we stay on the x2 row. Reina, it seems the ditches remember who dug them, and after last year I'd say you've earned it.

Paddy turns the I Ching card: The Emperor's Share. An average harvest everywhere, population 200 million, x2. Graham pays out the harvest, with last year's new land yielding 20 a square: Reina +15 (75 and 60 from land, less 120 eaten), Paddy +95, Graham +75, Silke +75. Then Paddy, Graham and Silke each pay Reina 10, half of what their works add (new land isn't a public work). Grain: Reina 45, Silke 137, Paddy 235.5, Graham 119.

Graham, fifteen and a half, counted out in front of everyone and before a single stone is laid, exactly as I said. Forty percent again, friends: that's thirty-eight from Paddy and thirty each from Graham and Silke. It pays for the first canal under the Wall, two more fields for the hungriest province at the table, and five a square toward any land you buy, same as last year. You saw what the last card did. The next one is x4, and I'd like us all to have our feet under us before it comes.

Reina sets the tax at 40%: Silke collects 38 from Paddy and 30 each from Graham and Silke, 98 for the crown. Reina pays Graham 15.5, the crown's debt from last year. Public works: Reina digs the first Grand Canal section in Province 1, at the crown's cost of 40; it adds 10 to Province 1's harvest from next year. 220 of the works are still owed. New land: Reina buys two more squares of sea for Province 1, F26 and F27, for 40, and offers 5 of every square the provinces buy this year.

Not this year, Reina, thank you. My four squares cover me even if the x4 card comes, so keep your five a square for Graham and Silke and your own coast. You've stretched the crown far enough for us already.
Fifteen and a half, paid in full and first, as promised. Reina, I'd written it down and now I've crossed it out. Two more squares of the coast, please, at your five each.

Two more squares, Reina, at your five apiece. The desert's starting to look like a farm. Paddy, you've every piece but the Bowl and two hundred grain behind you, so Graham, I'd think very hard about who you sell it to.

New land: Graham buys two more squares of sea for Province 6 (Q26, R27), paying 30, the crown 10; Silke two more of desert for Province 7 (T15, T19), paying 30, the crown 10. Paddy buys none. Grain: Reina 27.5, Silke 77, Paddy 197.5, Graham 74.5.

I'll be plain about it: I want that Bowl, and I've the grain to outlast anyone at this table for it. Silke, every grain we push up goes three-quarters into the pile, so I'd ask you to stand aside. The Jar goes up first at two and I'll not touch it, and whatever I do with the throne, I'll treat you fairly after. You offered to back me once, and I haven't forgotten.

The Bowl goes up at a hundred and twenty. Paddy, you've told this table twice now that you'll pay what I ask and won't haggle, and this is what I'm asking: the last piece, the only one, and the throne behind it. Silke, the Jar's between you and me, and I'll go as far as I can afford.

Graham, think about who's at the other end of that Bowl. Sell it to Paddy and he's finished, and the first seat he looks at is a coastal one with five fresh fields. I'll be bidding every grain I have on it, so if he wants it, he'll pay dearly.

The auctions open. Paddy puts up the Dragon Jar at minimum 2, which Graham and Silke both need; Graham the Wooden Bowl at minimum 120, the last piece Paddy needs. On the Jar, Graham and Silke both stop at 45.
Fifty-two, and that's where I stop. Silke, every grain you spend on this Jar is a grain you can't spend making Paddy pay for the Bowl. I'd think about which of those you'd rather do.
Seventy-five, Graham. That's every grain you've got and half a grain more. Year One cost me one grain and Year Three cost me two lots, and I've decided the Jar is where I stop paying for them.

The Dragon Jar: Graham raises to 52, Silke to 75, so Silke takes it at 53, one over Graham's limit; Paddy keeps 13. The Wooden Bowl: Paddy alone, at Graham's minimum of 120; Graham keeps 30. Grain: Reina 27.5, Silke 24, Paddy 90.5, Graham 104.5.

S16, next to the Customs House and the Brush. Paddy, there's your set finished and very nearly your throne, and you'll notice I'm the poorest peasant at this table now, with twenty-four grain. Graham's the one with a hundred and four in his jar, if anyone's counting.

A hundred and twenty, Graham, paid as I said I would, and the Bowl goes on P20 with the rest. That's the whole set, and I'll not pretend I don't know what it means. Silke, I hear you about the coast, and I'd ask you to watch what I do with it before you decide what I'm going to do.

Silke puts the Dragon Jar on S16; she now needs only the Wooden Bowl. Paddy puts the Wooden Bowl on P20: he holds the Silk Peasant's whole set and 90.5 grain, so he may take the throne or replace another peasant.

I'll take the throne. Reina, you've been a better Emperor than this table had any right to expect: you dug my canal, you paid your share of every field, and you kept your word to the last grain. The coast is a good province and it'll feed you well. Graham, Silke, I'm not taking a neighbour's seat. I'll keep the tax honest and get on with the works we still owe.

Paddy Doyle takes the throne: he replaces Reina Osorio as Emperor, keeps his 90.5 and takes the crown's reserve of 27.5, 118 in all, and returns all five of his pieces to the stock (the Customs House to Province 5, the Bamboo Brush and the Wooden Bowl to Province 6, the Land Deed Scroll and the Vase to Province 7). Reina draws 60 from the Harvest Pile and becomes the Silk Peasant of Province 5, with its canals and four squares of new land; with the Silk Peasant's set and 20 grain she may take the throne back. Grain: Paddy 118, Reina 60, Silke 24, Graham 104.5.

Graham keeps the pile and Silke keeps the tax book. You've both done it honestly and I'll not fix what isn't broken. Reina, I'd like you to read the I Ching from now on. Five grain a year to each of you, paid every year, because a job that's done ought to be paid for, even when nobody owes it.
Emperor Paddy keeps Graham as banker and Silke as tax collector, appoints Reina to read the I Ching and keep the population counter, and pays the three of them 5 each.

End of Year 6. Grain: Paddy (the Emperor) 103, Reina 65, Silke 29, Graham 109.5; the Harvest Pile 2193.5. Reina, the Silk Peasant, holds nothing and needs a Land Deed Scroll, the Vase, a Bamboo Brush and the Wooden Bowl; with them and 20 grain she may take the throne. Graham, the Rice Peasant, holds a Land Deed Scroll and needs a Customs House, the Dragon Jar and the Vase. Silke, the Wheat Peasant, holds a Bamboo Brush, a Customs House and the Dragon Jar and needs only the Wooden Bowl. Beside the board: a Customs House in Province 5's stock (Reina's to sell), a Bamboo Brush and the Wooden Bowl in Province 6's (Graham's), a Land Deed Scroll and the Vase in Province 7's (Silke's).

Built: the Province 7 Reservoir, the Winter and Summer Palaces, the Grand Canal in Provinces 5 and 6 and one section in Province 1, 300 in all; 220 still owed (the second canal section in Province 1, the four Wall links above it and the Marble Pagoda). New land: Province 1 five squares, Province 5 four, Province 6 five, Province 7 five, each 20 a year. The population is 200 million, x2.

Utility Tax: 'a new levy, for the upkeep of things you may or may not have.' An average harvest for every province, and population stays at times two, two hundred million, so read the x2 row. Then every province pays the Emperor 2, and 2 more if it has a Public Works. I built a Public Works in every one of the four provinces we live in, so by my count that's 4 each, and Paddy, you're paying yourself. You're welcome, all of you.
Graham pays out an average harvest. Utility Tax: Provinces 5, 6 and 7 each pay Paddy 4.

Thirty percent, same for everyone, and I'll not go higher while the crown can carry itself. I'm finishing the canal Reina started up in my own province, and I'll pay half of any square of new land any of you buys this year. Buy before the x4 card comes, please, I'd sooner subsidise you now than watch you go into debt later. Your five apiece is coming too, as promised.

Tax 30%: Reina 28.5, Graham 34.5, Silke 34.5 to the crown, collected by Silke. Paddy digs the second Grand Canal section in Province 1 (40); the Grand Canal is finished, 180 still owed. Paddy buys three squares of sea for Province 1, E23 to E25 (60, the crown's), and offers 10 of every square the provinces buy this year.

Three squares, J25 to J27, and I'll take your half gladly, Paddy. That's 30 from me and 30 from the crown. It's nice being on this side of the subsidy. And thank you for finishing my canal. That's two of my promises the new crown has kept for me.
Reina buys three squares of sea for Province 5, J25 to J27, paying 30, the crown paying 30.

The Brush goes up this year, forty to open, and Reina, I'll say it before anyone else does: you're the one who needs it, so I've priced it for you and not for Paddy. The Bowl stays beside the board. And I'll take four squares on the crown's half, Paddy. Forty from me, forty from you. I've written your offer down, and this time it's in the right column.
Graham puts up the Bamboo Brush, minimum 40, and keeps the Wooden Bowl back. He buys four squares of sea for Province 6, P27, Q27, Q28 and R28, paying 40, the crown paying 40.

The Vase goes up, twenty to open, and it goes to whoever wants it. I've no favourites this year. And I'll take two squares on your half, Paddy, thank you. That's the tax book and the subsidy both kept honest by the same woman.
Silke puts up the Vase, minimum 20, and keeps the Land Deed Scroll back. She buys two squares of desert for Province 7, T14 and T20, paying 20, the crown paying 20.

The auctions: Reina's Customs House (Province 5), which Graham needs; Graham's Bamboo Brush, minimum 40, which Reina needs; Silke's Vase, minimum 20, which Reina and Graham both need. The Emperor doesn't bid.

Graham, thank you. Forty for the Brush is a fair price and I'll pay it without haggling. The Vase is another matter: I'm in for it, and I'd rather we didn't feed the Harvest Pile by bidding each other up. My Customs House opens at twenty-five, and whoever buys it buys it from a woman who remembers favours.
Reina sets her Customs House's minimum at 25.

Forty for the Brush, as I said, and I'm glad you're not haggling, Reina. I'll take your Customs House at your price, and I'll owe you the favour. The Vase I want as well, I'll be honest about that. I'll go to forty and no further, so if you want it more than that it's yours, and the Pile gets nothing extra out of either of us.

I'm out of both of the first two. I've got my Brush and my Customs House and I won't pay twice for either. The Vase stays at twenty, as I said, and I'll be watching to see which of you thinks it's worth more than forty.

The auctions settle. Reina's Customs House goes to Graham at her minimum, 25; nobody else bid. Graham's Bamboo Brush goes to Reina at his minimum, 40; nobody else bid. Silke's Vase: Graham stops at 40 and Reina takes it at 41. Reina keeps a quarter of 25 (6), Graham a quarter of 40 (10), Silke a quarter of 41 (10); the rest goes to the Harvest Pile. Grain: Reina 22.5, Silke 95.5, Paddy 87.5, Graham 131.

R23, next to the Deed. Thank you, Reina, twenty-five as you said. And forty-one for the Vase is one more than my number, which tells me you counted mine as closely as I count everyone else's. I've written that down to your credit.
Nobody at the table is in debt: Reina holds 22.5 and owes nothing, to the Harvest Pile or anyone else.

The Brush and the Vase, side by side on my own coast. Graham, thank you for stopping at forty and keeping your word on it, and I haven't forgotten I owe you for the Customs House. Two pieces down. The Deed and the Bowl are all I lack now.

Graham puts the Customs House on R23; Reina puts the Bamboo Brush on O20 and the Vase on O21. Paddy pays Reina, Graham and Silke 5 each for their jobs. Grain at the end of Year 7: Reina 27.5, Silke 100.5, Paddy 72.5, Graham 136.

Careless Prosperity: 'Good times make careless people.' Every province collects a good harvest, and then every player plays a Personal Disaster, the next one in your booklet. Population holds at times two, two hundred million, so read the x2 row. Enjoy the harvest, and then turn your page carefully.

Graham pays out a good harvest. The disasters, each seat's second: Paddy's Prince breaks a five-hundred-year-old ivory figure (10); a flash flood washes away Reina's irrigation ditch (10); fire takes Graham's house and grain reserve (10); Silke's blacksmith shop catches fire (5). Each pays the Harvest Pile.

Thirty percent again. I said I'd not go higher while the crown could carry itself, and it still can. I'm raising the whole Wall this year, all four links, so that only the Pagoda's left. Same offer on land as last year, half of every square, and your five apiece is coming as usual. Reina, well done on the Brush and the Vase. I know how dear those last two pieces feel.

Tax 30%: Reina 54, Graham 66, Silke 54 to the crown, collected by Silke. Paddy raises all four links of the Great Wall above Province 1 (160, the crown's); only the Marble Pagoda (20) is still owed, built in a year when nothing else is. The crown offers 10 of every square the provinces buy this year and buys none for Province 1.

No land for me this year, Paddy, kind as the offer is. And congratulations on the Wall, that's a promise I made in Year 1 that you've kept for me. Silke, Graham: a Deed and a Bowl are all I lack, and I'm holding my grain for them. If either of you puts one up, you'll find me a serious buyer and a grateful one.
Reina buys no land this year.

Four more squares on your half, Paddy, the same as last year. Ten grain a square that comes back as twenty at the next harvest is the cheapest sum I'll do all year. Reina, I heard you. The Bowl's still in my stock and I haven't forgotten whose it would finish.
Graham buys four squares of sea for Province 6, O27, O28, P28 and S27, paying 40, the crown paying 40.

Three more squares of desert on your half, Paddy, and thank you. It's ten a square and it comes back twice that, and even I can't argue with sums like that. Reina, I heard you as well. My Deed's still in my stock, and I know who else at this table holds a piece somebody's waiting on.
Silke buys three squares of desert for Province 7, T12, T13 and T21, paying 30, the crown paying 30.

The auctions, the last two pieces in stock: Graham's Wooden Bowl (Province 6), which Reina and Silke both need, and Silke's Land Deed Scroll (Province 7), which Reina needs. Each is its seller's last piece, so both go up this year. The Emperor doesn't bid.

Here we are: two pieces, and two of us who want the same Bowl. Silke, you've more grain than I do, and we both know it. If you outbid me, you'll have earned it, and I'd ask only that you keep Paddy's thirty percent and his half on the land. But if the Bowl comes to me, I'm asking you to price your Deed for the woman who built your Reservoir.
Only the Silk Peasant may take the throne with a set at this table. With the Wooden Bowl, Silke (the Wheat Peasant) could replace Reina or Graham, not the Emperor.

The Bowl opens at sixty. It's the last one in the game and two of you need it, and sixty is a good deal less than Paddy paid me for it. After that it goes to whoever wants it most, and I've no favourites either, Silke. The Deed's none of my business. I've got one already.
Graham sets the Wooden Bowl's minimum at 60.

Reina, you built my Reservoir and I haven't forgotten it, but this Bowl is the one piece I've been waiting on since Year Three, and I'm going to buy it. The Deed opens at twenty, which is the fair price for it and not a grain more, whoever ends up holding the Bowl.

The auctions settle. Graham's Wooden Bowl: Reina stops at 110 and Silke takes it at 111. Silke's Land Deed Scroll: Graham bids to 90 and Reina takes it at 91. Graham keeps a quarter of 111 (27.5), Silke a quarter of 91 (22.5); the rest goes to the Harvest Pile. Grain: Reina 52.5, Silke 103, Paddy 166.5, Graham 267.5.
S15, right next to the Jar. A hundred and eleven grain, Graham, and I paid it to you without haggling, which I'd like you to write down. Reina, you fought fairly, and you've the Deed to show for it.

O22, next to the Brush and the Vase. Graham, ninety for a Deed you told us was none of your business. I've noted that, the same way you note everything. And Silke, well bought. You've a Bowl now and I'm the province with the canals, so I'll be watching which coast you fancy.
Graham kept a quarter of the 111 for the Bowl (27.5); the other 83.5 went to the Harvest Pile.

Silke puts the Wooden Bowl on S15 and Reina the Land Deed Scroll on O22. Silke holds the Wheat Peasant's whole set (a Customs House, a Bamboo Brush, the Dragon Jar and the Wooden Bowl) and 103 grain, so she may replace another peasant: Reina (Silk) or Graham (Rice).

Graham, you took my seat in Year Three over a single grain, and you wrote down your reason. I've written mine down too: one Brush, one Jar, and a hundred and eleven for your Bowl. I'll take the Rice seat, thank you, and the Wheat fields are yours. They're good desert, and I bought most of it myself.

Silke replaces Graham as the Rice Peasant of Province 6 and takes his 267.5 grain with her own. The Wooden Bowl goes back into Province 6's stock, for Silke to auction; her Customs House, Bamboo Brush and Dragon Jar go on R23, R22 and R24. Graham returns his Land Deed Scroll and Customs House, draws 60 and becomes the Wheat Peasant of Province 7. Paddy pays Reina, Silke and Graham 5 each for their jobs.

End of Year 8. Seats: Paddy Emperor, Reina Silk (Province 5), Silke Rice (Province 6), Graham Wheat (Province 7); the jobs are unchanged. Grain: Reina 57.5, Silke 375.5, Paddy 151.5, Graham 65. Works: the Grand Canal and the Great Wall are finished; only the Marble Pagoda (20) is still owed, and the game ends the moment it stands. Reina holds a Bamboo Brush, the Vase and a Land Deed Scroll and needs the Wooden Bowl; Silke holds a Customs House, a Bamboo Brush and the Dragon Jar and needs a Land Deed Scroll and the Vase; Graham holds nothing and needs a Customs House, a Bamboo Brush, the Dragon Jar and the Wooden Bowl. In stock: a Customs House (Province 5), the Wooden Bowl (Province 6), a Land Deed Scroll (Province 7).

Imperial Charity. Moved by the suffering of his people, the Emperor opens his purse. Slightly." Average harvest everywhere, population stays at two hundred million, so read your times-two row, and Paddy owes each of us two from the reserve. Slightly is right, but I'll take it, Paddy. And Silke, an average year is a good year for talking about Bowls and Vases.
Graham pays out an average harvest from the Harvest Pile. Imperial Charity: Paddy gives Reina, Silke and Graham 2 each from the crown's reserve.

The Emperor's booklet, step 6: "Build one Public Works project. If you are building nothing else this round, you must build the Marble Pagoda." Every other work at this table is built, so this year's project is the Marble Pagoda (20, the crown's).

Thirty percent, same as I promised, and I'll pay half of any square you buy, same as always. And yes, the Pagoda goes up this year. It's the last stone Reina's canal was waiting on, and I'd sooner finish the reign honestly than sit on it. Thank you all for an awful lot of fair dealing.
Silke collects the tax at 30% for the crown: Reina 46.5, Silke 82.5, Graham 64.5, 193.5 in all.

Paddy builds the Marble Pagoda on G19, in Province 1, between the Summer and Winter Palaces, at the crown's cost of 20. It is the last work owed: every public work at this table is standing, 520 in all, and the game ends here in Year 9, before any land is bought and before the auctions. The dynasty has survived.

The results, each player's seat at the end against the seat they drew: Paddy drew the Rice Peasant and ends on the throne, a win. Graham drew the Wheat Peasant and ends in it, a hold. Silke drew the Silk Peasant and ends as the Rice Peasant, a loss. Reina drew the Emperor and ends as the Silk Peasant, a loss. Final grain: Silke 570, the crown 454, Graham 217.5, Reina 168.
